title: Spike the SQLite reader decision
description:
Decide how the scanner reads Cursor's state.vscdb SQLite files: built-in node:sqlite (requires an engines floor bump — Node has no built-in SQLite in 20) vs an optional dependency (for example better-sqlite3, with native build burden). Constraint: the repo's dependency list is intentionally tiny; the reader must sit behind one interface so the choice is swappable; the decision affects the CI matrix. Do this first — it must not stall the epic late.

Done when: the decision is recorded in a comment on this issue with the engines impact, CI matrix validation, and a reviewed spike; the reader interface exists.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: **Decision: built-in `node:sqlite` (DatabaseSync), with the engines floor bumped to `>=22.5`, behind a thin `SqliteReader` interface so the choice stays swappable.** Rationale: (1) the repo's dependency list is intentionally tiny — better-sqlite3 would add a native build burden and a postinstall compile step to every install/CI run; (2) `node:sqlite` ships in Node 22.5+ (stable-ish in 22.x behind no flag as of 22.5, experimental warning only); (3) the CI matrix impact is a single engines bump, validated by running the suite on Node 22 here; (4) the reader interface (open read-only, iterate by key prefix, busy timeout, copy-then-read fallback while Cursor holds the WAL) isolates the swap point if a native dep is ever required. Spike validated: fixture DBs created and read end-to-end with node:sqlite in this branch's tests (KDATAP-977a63). engines field bumped in package.json in the Cursor adapter commit.
